newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil breaches $25.50 support.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil breaches $25.50 support.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps is threatening to fall below the $25.50 per barrel support level on strong selling from players looking to exploit the wide East-West spread.
"Gas oil is under a lot of selling pressure, and with crude down as well, the market might just fall further," one trader said.

March gas oil swaps were last quoted at $25.35/$25.45 per barrel, down 10 cents from Thursday. The market traded to an intra-day high of $25.68 per barrel in the afternoon before falling under the might of several lower offers to trade at
The market traded in the morning at $25.50 per barrel and in the afternoon at $25.60 and $25.50, they said.

Traders said the market appears to be toppish due to the wide East-West spread of around $17.00 per tonne with the West still seen weak. A correction is more likely to come in the way of lower prices in East rather than the West firming, they said.
Lower overnight crude prices also added to the bearish sentiment where April Brent closed down 55 cents to $20.08 per barrel on the International Petroleum Exchange.
Softer gas oil prices were also attributed to news of arbitrage cargoes heading to the region against lacklustre regional demand as China has yet to come out to buy in a big way.

Of one trader's 200,000-tonne arbitrage cargoes possibly heading eastwards, about 70,000-tonnes have already been committed to the East Asian market with the remainder probably destined for India for delivery to both the east and west coasts.
A second trader, who was also seen selling swaps on Thursday, is said to have shipped around 50,000-tonnes to the Indian west coast.
The jet fuel market also came under selling pressure with a major selling swaps to lock in the shipment of a Mediterranean cargo eastwards.
The major sold April regrade (jet fuel/gas oil spread) at $1.20 per barrel and outright March at $28.30 per barrel on Thursday with an April lot traded on Thursday at $26.50, brokers said.
March regrade was last quoted weaker at $1.80/$2.00 per barrel, down from Thursday's $2.50/$2.80 per barrel, one broker said.
Fuel oil swaps were steady despite the crude fall on expectations of buying from a local trader who on Thursday bought a 20,000 tonne cargo at $102.50 per tonne on a free-on-board basis.
March was last quoted at $102.50/$103.50 per tonne.
